links.comparator_used: Baseline prompt with no readability control (fixed output not adapted to the question's readability)
links.outcome: Agreement between question readability and response readability (quadratic-weighted Cohen kappa)
links.effect: External calculator-guided strategy had the highest agreement: Gemini 3 κ=0.94; GPT 5.2 κ=0.90. Response accuracy stayed >98% for GPT 5.2 and Gemini 3, and BERTScore F1 stayed >0.87.
links.tradeoff: The open-source OSS-20b model had lower accuracy (83.75%-90%) and was more sensitive to readability constraints. Longer questions were associated with slightly lower accuracy in lower-performing configurations.
links.quote: The external calculator-guided strategy produced the strongest alignment in readability across models, achieving the highest agreement (Gemini 3: κ=0.94; GPT 5.2: κ=0.90), while maintaining favorable computational efficiency.

links.comparator_used: Semantic Readability Inference (LLM estimating readability itself) and Formula-Informed Readability Prompt
links.outcome: Agreement between question and response readability (quadratic-weighted Cohen kappa)
links.effect: The external calculator-guided prompt gave the strongest alignment (Gemini 3 κ=0.94; GPT 5.2 κ=0.90). Formula-informed prompting was intermediate. Semantic inference gave poor agreement.
links.quote: Formula-informed prompting showed intermediate performance, whereas semantic inference demonstrated poor agreement due to unreliable readability estimation.

design_hint: reading-level constraints and readability prompting strategies
